thread:
alex_w: ran an nsys capture on the 2pm canary after the kernel-selection tweak. seeing frequent kernel rebinds during single requests and a correlated drop in KV/prefix cache hits.

maria_r: hmm. which tweak? the new prefer_gemm_for_short flag we merged earlier?

alex_w: yeah. trace looks like: ```
nsys: timeline
seq  kernel         start_ms   end_ms   notes
18   aten_gemm      120.3      121.0
19   kv_lookup      121.1      121.2   (miss)
20   aten_gemm_fast 121.25     121.6   (switched kernel)
21   kv_insert      121.7      121.8
22   aten_gemm      121.9      122.4
```

alex_w: every time the runtime switches kernel variants mid-request we lose the warm KV cache path (prefix reuse fails) and we get a bunch of misses for the next 4-8 tokens. overall hit rate dropped from ~92% -> ~58% on shared-prefix benchmark.

sam_k: oof. that explains the latency tail too. P50 stable, p99 jump. numbers?

priya_s: aggregated from the canary:
- before: KV hit 92.1%, avg latency 78ms, p99 210ms
- after:  KV hit 58.3%, avg latency 92ms, p99 460ms
- batch size distribution shifted: more small batches (1-2) due to new policy

perf-bot: [regression-alert] perf/regressions/2054321000 -> KV-hit-drop 33.8% (severity: high). See perfboard: https://perf.internal/redwood/2054321000

maria_r: the prefer_gemm_for_short path changes kernel selection heuristics to favor fused kernels for seq<64. but it doesn't check whether the active KV cache layout matches the kernel execution path. so if we pick a different kernel we end up taking a different codepath that bypasses the cached prefix helper.

alex_w: right — we often do fast-paths that assume a certain KV layout (packed vs interleaved). switching invalidates assumptions.

sam_k: quick mitigation: prevent kernel variant switch if there's a recent KV hit sequence for the request. e.g. if last_kv_hits > 3 and seq_pos < 64, prefer current kernel. cheap guard.

priya_s: I ran a microbenchmark with that guard locally:
- with guard: KV hit 89.7%, p99 225ms
- without guard: KV hit 59.2%, p99 470ms

alex_w: can we push a tiny canary hotfix that adds that guard? less invasive than rolling back the whole flag.

maria_r: yes. will add a low-risk check in kernel_selector: if request_prefix_reuse_ratio > 0.3 and pending_batch_count >= 1 -> lock kernel.

sam_k: patch uploaded to PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/789 (small change in kernel_selector.cc). also added an nsys capture test harness.

perf-bot: automated smoke on canary queued (nsys capture + kv-stats) — will post results here.

priya_s: I'll run a targeted perfetto capture across the canary fleet at 2054321200, capturing NVTX ranges for kv_lookup/kv_insert so we can validate timeline stays contiguous.

alex_w: sounds good. if the guard fixes it we keep prefer_gemm_for_short. if not we rollback.

maria_r: one more thought: batching heuristics shifted to prefer latency -> smaller batches. smaller batches mean less opportunity for prefix reuse across requests in the same batch. we should log batch-size + kv-hit correlation to dashboards.

sam_k: adding a metric: batch_size_histogram + kv_hit_by_batch_size. I'll wire it to the console.

priya_s: capture finished. perf-bot posted artifacts: nsys/timeline + kv-stats. initial look shows the kernel rebind frequency reduced ~80% with the guard.

alex_w: nice. thumbs up. :thumbsup:

maria_r: deploy patch to canary and monitor for 1h, then roll to the main pool if stable. :eyes:

perf-bot: canary run results: KV hit back to 90.4%, p99 218ms, no further regressions detected.

alex_w: thanks everyone. follow-up: sam, add the batch-size -> kv-hit dashboard; priya, add a perftest with tiny seqs to catch future kernel-switch-induced misses; maria, open a follow-up to formalize kernel/kv compatibility checks.

sam_k: on it.

priya_s: will do.

maria_r: created follow-up issue #1423: kernel-selector: enforce KV layout compatibility and telemetry.

alex_w: closing thread. great triage & fast fix. :tada:
